_comment: Single machine-readable home for finance-pipeline constants (spec T6/T30/T32/T36). Prose/design rationale lives in vault/knowledge/design-finance-blockframe.md — never duplicate it here.

en._chars_per_second_note: 17.57 is tuned for MEDIUM/LONG. ⚠ A SHORT cut will run ~9% long on this key — re-measure before trusting it. Provenance: vault/workflows/voiceover-tts.md.

cuts._note: US/$ only since 2026-08-15. The Hindi cut and @cashguruguides are retired; `en` is the sole cut and every stage is single-cut. History: vault/knowledge/channels.md §D.

tts._pause_seconds_note: Silence the voice actually takes at each mark, added to the flat chars/rate estimate in pipeline_check.expected_seconds. Without it a punched cold-open self-flags as truncated.

tiers._tier_seconds_note: The tier's own target is named differently per tier by design — short `default_target_seconds` (a default inside a range), medium `target_seconds` (fixed), long `min_seconds` (a floor). Anything computing a budget must read the one its tier declares.
tiers._max_sfx_cues_note: A cue budget, not a target: a sound is punctuation, and if every reveal has one then none of them means anything. Only the SHORT number is earned (≤10 on a 165 s cut, creator-era rule); MEDIUM and LONG are that same ~3.6 cues/min rate carried to their targets, because the SHORT figure taken literally gives a 9:29 chapter cut one transition for 86 scene boundaries. Kit and per-sound discipline: tools/audio/kit.json.
tiers._comparable_length_band_note: What counts as a COMPARABLE video when studying competitors. backend/study.py hard-filters below MIN_DURATION_SEC = 240 s (it is a general vault tool and does not read this file), so the SHORT band lies entirely under its floor — short-tier comparables come from vidIQ, not from a study packet. The ceiling is what this key adds: a 40-minute video is not a comparable for an 8:30 cut.

script._note: Length and pacing constants the script/audit gates enforce. They span tier and cut (a budget needs both), which is why they are not inside `tiers` or `cuts`.
script.char_budget_formula: chars = <the tier's target seconds, per tiers._tier_seconds_note> × cuts.<cut>.chars_per_second. A cut passes at ±length_tolerance_pct of that. fin-audit gate one enforces it and must READ this, not re-derive it: a gate that invents the rule it enforces can only ever agree with itself.
script._hook_gate_note: The payoff promise — the line that says what the viewer gets, not the number that proves it — must have STARTED by this mark. Measured on the rendered clip with silencedetect and recorded in run.json as hook_gate_<cut>, never modelled from char counts: on passive-income-number the flat model said 10.9-13.0 s and the pause-loaded model ~15.5 s for the same line. 15 s was assumed for four cuts before it was written down here and happened to be right. Both cuts must gate on the SAME object or the number compares nothing.
script._mid_roll_note: YouTube's mid-roll eligibility floor. MEDIUM targets 510 s to clear it with 30 s of margin, which is why a MEDIUM overrun is harmless and an UNDERRUN is not — a 2% miss on the wrong side costs the ad break, and nothing else about the cut changes.
script._chars_per_word_note: MEASURED 2026-08-15 across all seven shipped -en scripts (45,802 VO chars / 8,130 words), not a textbook average — per-script range 5.50-5.94, and the two shortest scripts pull highest, so a SHORT cut budgets a little conservatively at this key. Exists so a word count can be converted to the char budget the gate actually enforces. Re-measure if the register changes materially; a 50+ audience using terms of art (IRMAA, distribution, beneficiary) will drift this UP, which shortens the word budget for the same runtime.
script.word_budget_formula: words = ((the tier's target seconds) - lines x (lead_in_seconds + tail_seconds)) x chars_per_second / chars_per_word. Creator decision 2026-08-15: keep Brian at his measured 17.57 c/s and WRITE LONGER, rather than slowing the voice. The plan's 140 wpm is retired as a budgeting input — it describes a delivery pace this voice does not have.
script._word_budget_worked: At 17.57 c/s and 5.63 c/word the voice delivers 3.121 words per second OF AUDIO. Padding is charged per LINE and is not audio, so it must come off the target first - that subtraction is the whole difference between a script that passes gate one and one that overruns. Worked: MEDIUM 510s/78 lines -> 447.6s audio -> 7,864 chars -> ~1,397 words. 9:00/540s at ~85 lines -> 472.0s -> 8,293 chars -> ~1,473 words. LONG 600s/92 lines -> 526.4s audio -> 9,249 chars -> ~1,643 words. Tolerance is script.length_tolerance_pct.

scene._transition_note: Cross-dissolve length. EVERY scene but the last carries data-duration = its duration + this, so the outgoing scene is still on screen while the incoming one fades in. Root duration is unaffected. See tools/scaffold/assets/js/motion.js.
scene._scene_seconds_note: Scene COUNT is emergent from the script (one VO line = one clip = one scene), never a constant. These bound felt pace: aim ~6.5s, and check_build FAILS a scene holding one photo past max_scene_seconds. `lines: 9` is a SHORT-tier constant only.
scene._no_max_hold_seconds: There is no `scene.max_hold_seconds` and there must not be — it would be a second home for a number that already has two precise ones. A STILL frame with no motion on it: max_static_hold_seconds. A whole scene, motion included: max_scene_seconds. Reach for the one you mean.

assets._note: Acceptance floors for a sourced photograph. Every one of these is enforced in tools/pipeline_check.py check_assets — they live here so the stage that FETCHES can honour them at fetch time, which is the only cheap moment: none of the three is fixable after the pick.
assets._min_source_yhigh_note: 90th-percentile luma of the SOURCE still (ffprobe signalstats YHIGH). Under the chapter archetype layer the grade is locked (grayscale .32 / brightness .62) and per-scene filter overrides are forbidden, so a source with no highlights has nothing for the grade to leave behind. Calibrated on the 20 promoted images of passive-income-number-hi ch1+ch2, not on one bad frame: s4 = 93 (failed by eye twice), a 30-point gap to s11b = 123 (looked at, passed), everything else ≥134. ONE-SIDED ON PURPOSE — the opposite failure (a high-key flat texture reading as a UI panel, ch2's s16 at 242) is real but luma does not predict it: ch2's s10 measures 246 and reads fine, because numerals and red pins give it structure. That one still needs eyes. Chapter mode only; plain blockframe keeps the inline filter escape hatch.
assets._min_width_note: 1600 is the floor for any scene that gets a long full-bleed zoom — 1280 was first-lakh-first-thousand's library norm and the hook hit ~1.6× upscale, soft at 1:1. Only Pexels clears it (`--pick` returns 1880 at dpr=2&w=940; Pixabay's largeImageURL is 1280), so a zoom or hero-number slot picks the pool by this key, independent of the dedupe reason to switch pools.

_architectures_note: The pipeline ROTATES these — `pipeline_check.py architecture --tier <t>` returns the least recently used, written into run.json before fin-script. Add an entry to put a new layout into the rotation. EVERY entry declares the tier it belongs to, and the rotation only ever considers entries of the RUNNING tier: these are all `short`, so at MEDIUM/LONG `tiers.<tier>.architecture` wins and the rotation (and the lock) do not apply. Without that rule a MEDIUM run recorded `architecture: blockframe-9` in run.json while its tier said per-line-chapters, and nothing said which the build should follow.
_architecture_lock_note: When set, this WINS over the rotation and every run OF ITS OWN TIER uses it; a run at another tier never sees it. Delete the key to resume rotating; `doctor` refuses a lock naming an architecture that does not exist. Why blockframe-9 is locked: vault/knowledge/design-finance-blockframe.md §0.
_image_per_scene_note: HARD creator rule: every architecture MUST declare image_per_scene: true and carry a photograph in EVERY frame. `doctor` refuses one without it. Pairs with layout.photo_free_scene_ratio = 0.
_stock_video_note: Footage behind a scene is SUPPORTED and shipped; HyperFrames pre-extracts frames so rendering stays deterministic. Mechanism and evidence: vault/knowledge/design-finance-blockframe.md.

video_scene._note: Load-bearing rules for footage behind a scene. The first one is the trap: it renders BLACK and no linter catches it.
video_scene.must_be_root_child: A <video> MUST be a direct child of #root. Our .bg is a div inside <section class='scene'> — a <video> placed there renders black. Hoist footage to root siblings and give that scene's .scene background: transparent, or its opaque --bg paints over the footage.
video_scene.no_ken_on_video: Never apply `ken` to footage — real camera motion and a Ken Burns push fight each other.
video_scene._duration_note: A clip shorter than its scene freezes on its last frame. Scenes run 11-28s and stock clips 8-20s, so pre-loop at fetch time with ffmpeg rather than discovering it at render.

vector_art._note: Icons and flat-illustration Lotties. Both sit ON the graded photograph, never instead of it (image_per_scene is a hard rule). Rationale, licence and the two silent-blank traps: vault/knowledge/design-icons-emoji-lottie.md. Components: .icon / .lottie / .aside in blockframe.css. Motion: draw / loadLottie / playLottie in motion.js.
vector_art.library: assets/ — git-tracked, OUTSIDE studio/ (which is gitignored and deleted per cut). REUSE BEFORE YOU FETCH: search the library first, and save back anything you had to fetch or draw, so the next video finds it locally. assets/lottie/<name>.json (pristine, untinted) + <name>.png (preview) + index.json (tags/source/licence/used_in); assets/icons/<name>.svg. See assets/README.md.
vector_art.icon_first: An icon, arrow, chart mark or currency glyph is an inline <svg class='icon'> animated with draw() — no player, no asset, and the stroke takes a palette colour via currentColor. Reach for Lottie only when the graphic is a real illustration that would take an hour to rebuild.
vector_art.emoji: Not the icon system. A colour emoji renders correctly but is an OS font (tofu on a machine without one) and sits outside the grade, so it reads as a sticker on a film. Deliberate tonal break only.

lottie.search: tools/lottie/search.py "<phrase>" --sheet — prints the LIBRARY matches first (with their own contact sheet) and only then the remote candidates. Fetching something the library already holds is the failure mode this exists to prevent.
lottie.save_back: tools/lottie/search.py --save "<cell>=<name>" --tags "a,b,c" — writes the pristine asset into assets/lottie/. Do this BEFORE tinting: the library never stores a pre-coloured file, and an asset that skips this step is one the next video has to find again.
lottie.license: Lottie Simple License (free catalogue only): commercial use ok, modification ok, NO attribution required, must not redistribute the raw file. The premium marketplace needs a paid plan and is not used.
lottie.vector_only: Reject any asset whose assets[] carry a "p" (embedded bitmap) — it cannot be re-tinted and it will not scale to 1080p.
lottie.tint: tools/lottie/tint.py <library-name> studio/videos/<slug>-<cut>/assets/lottie/<n>.js <accent-hex> — REQUIRED. Stock art arrives in someone else's colours and lands on the grade as clip-art; the tint maps it onto a panel->accent->ink ramp by luminance. Accent = the scene's role colour (fund/target/warn).
lottie.loader: loadLottie() + playLottie() from motion.js. Never lottie.loadAnimation() directly, never window.__hfLottie, never a path: URL — each of those renders a blank scene that passes every check.
lottie.inline_as_js: assets/lottie/<name>.js assigning window.L_<name> = {...}. A .json fetched at runtime resolves after the runtime has inspected the page.
lottie._cap_note: PER CHAPTER, not per video (2026-08-04). The cap is the point at which you must justify the next one, not a target to hit.
lottie.reach_for_it_when: The beat is a NUMBER, COMPARISON, PROCESS, DATE, SHARE or COUNT — anything a photograph cannot state. A ratio (37.8% vs ~1%), a subset inside a set, a date being circled: these are FAILS as flat photos, not missed opportunities. Stock cannot photograph an abstraction; drawing it is the only honest option.
lottie.truth_bar: Drawn art asserts a measurement, so it carries a higher bar than a photograph. Heights, counts and proportions are computed from facts-staging figures and the generator says so in a comment. Anything reading as a published figure must BE one; a decorative proportion that looks like a statistic is a defect. Never fabricate a source document — no invented agency names, seals or legible figures on a frame cited to a real table.

blockframe-9.summary: Centred stack over a full-bleed graded photo. The original system.

swiss-band.summary: Swiss/Vignelli. A fixed 1920x600 photographic band on a 12-column grid, black title bar above, statement hung from a rule below. Flush left, squared corners, no scrim, no text-shadow, TWO type sizes per scene.
swiss-band.notes: The band is a fixed aperture — identical geometry every scene — which unifies nine unrelated photos geometrically instead of with a filter. Dense beats (chip rows, four-row bills, the two-column classifier) must be RESTRUCTURED to fit the 240px statement zone, not shrunk: two type sizes per scene is the rule, from the Vignelli Canon. Vary the aperture across the nine scenes as a sequence, never the same window nine times — that is the anti-sameness engine. Retire the per-scene --tint here: colour is a signifier, not pictorial.

ledger-rail.summary: 300px left rail carrying the scene index (thin weight) + beat label; content left-aligned and ragged right; photo confined to a hard-edged right panel, so no scrim and no text-shadow are needed.

cascade._note: A declared cascade is ONE focal group arriving in sequence, so it counts as a SINGLE element against max_simultaneous_elements (five chips are not five elements) and is the one exemption from cue_min_gap_seconds. Five items at max_chips_per_row: 3 is two rows; more rows than that is a table, and a table is a different frame.

layout.image_relevance: THE SOUND-OFF TEST (hard creator rule, 2026-08-04): with the sound off and the on-screen text stripped, the image alone must tell the viewer what the scene is about. Applied PER LINE, not per chapter — every point in the script got its own line because it is its own idea, so it gets its own picture. Three failures, all shipped at least once before this rule was written: (1) an image that argues with its line (a balanced scale under 'thirty times apart'); (2) one image reused across several points (one photo of books behind the internet claim, the survey AND the 30x gap); (3) an image asserting the wrong place or era (an Indian shopkeeper for Japan's national accounts, a demonetised Rs500 for today's money). When a slot cannot be photographed, change the SOURCE or draw it — never accept a near-miss: @commons for named buildings/institutions/monuments, a Lottie for abstractions.
layout.grade_note: blockframe.css ships .bg { grayscale(.32) brightness(.62) }. Per-scene overrides that go darker to make drawn art readable stack with it and desaturate real photographs into grey mush — the creator rejected exactly this on 2026-08-04 ('it fails to black and white'). If a Lottie needs a darker field, darken BEHIND THE ART, not the whole frame.

_known_benign_note: Empty is the correct state. ⚠ A lint ERROR makes `hyperframes check` SKIP the layout and contrast passes entirely, so an entry added to silence one hides two. Fix at the root instead. The one entry ever added was wrong — story in vault/knowledge/design-finance-blockframe.md §9.

qa._vad_note: Silero VAD reports onset LATE and quantised — subtract vad_onset_latency_seconds before comparing against the drift target, and re-measure it if the model or window changes.
qa._vo_drift_note: The master-QA drift gate, machine-run by `pipeline_check check render` since 2026-08-09 (it was four numeric thresholds inside fin-render's prompt). Each clip's timing.json audio_start is matched to the NEAREST VAD onset within vo_drift_match_window_seconds, not to the Nth onset — a line with an internal danda pause splits into two segments, so positional matching drifts by a whole line from there on. The window is under the 0.8s of inter-line padding, so two lines can never claim the same onset. Measured on both cuts of passive-income-number, 2026-08-09: max |drift| 0.049 s (hi ch2, 13 lines, 34 segments) and 0.055 s (en ch3, 16 lines), mean -0.008 / +0.021 — i.e. the 0.101 s latency constant is confirmed against real renders, and the 0.1 s target has real headroom.
qa._peak_dbtp_note: True-peak ceiling for the file that is UPLOADED (PUBLISH-, not the FINAL- master). tools/loudnorm.py aims at TP=-2.0 because AAC overshoots the limiter and the overshoot scales with SFX transients — its docstring carries the measurements. This key is the pass/fail line both loudnorm.py and check_render read, so the gate and the tool that has to satisfy it cannot drift apart.
qa._black_note: A black stretch this long is a dead frame, not a transition: chapter joints in the master are 0.45 s CROSS-DISSOLVES between two lit scenes and never reach black. Measured zero hits on the passive-income-number drafts.
qa._dissolve_note: Sample transitions at BOTH offsets: a midpoint frame lands before the incoming text exists and cannot see a double-paint.
qa._whisper_note: Whisper for COVERAGE (gaps, dropped clips), VAD for onsets. Whisper segment starts merge lines and produce phantom outliers.

chapter_design._note: The archetype layer for chapter-based (MEDIUM/LONG) cuts. Rationale and the full rule list: vault/knowledge/design-chapter-archetypes.md. Code: tools/scaffold/assets/chapter-design.css. Adopted 2026-08-05 after five draft passes on japanese-money-methods ch1+ch2, creator-approved.

A.use: centred stack, motif full-bleed behind — chapter opens, hand-offs

B.use: the figure owns the frame; rule at the left margin, measure bar under the type

C.use: hard vertical split — type left, artefact full-height right, cropped by the frame edge

D.use: type under a full-width rule, mechanism owning the bottom two-thirds

scene_modifiers.has-photo: REQUIRED on every scene carrying a graded still. Ground -> 38% tint, plate -> aperture, hatch off.
scene_modifiers.art-off: the scene's drawn layer duplicates the photograph; hide it. See rule 8.
scene_modifiers.art-forward: buy the drawn layer back to 52% — only for scenes whose point is a PROPORTION.
scene_modifiers.centred: the archetype's other side is empty, so the split is a hole; re-centre and drop plate/crule/vrule/brule.
scene_modifiers.art-lift: keep the plate's panel lift on a scene whose drawn layer sits on a BRIGHT still (ruled paper, banknotes, a white wardrobe). `.has-photo` turns the plate into an aperture, which is right over a dark photograph and makes ink art light-on-light over a pale one. This is the plate-scoped form of rule 9 — it darkens BEHIND the art and cannot touch the photograph outside the plate rect.

ken_safe_zone._note: The genuinely-always-visible svg window once ken scales the field 1.0->1.16. Art outside it is cropped silently and every check still passes. A .plate makes this moot by declaring its own window — prefer the plate.

art_opacity._important_note: `.has-photo .art` and `.has-photo.art-forward .art` both carry !important, so a per-scene inline opacity on the <svg> is a NO-OP. The only levers that reach the screen are the weight and alpha of the elements INSIDE it.

gotchas: stroke-width="N" as an SVG ATTRIBUTE is a no-op — .art .st sets it in CSS and a CSS rule always beats a presentation attribute. Use inline style="stroke-width:N".
A scrolling group needs a clipPath or it rides out of its band into the type.
breathe(dur) quantises to whole out-and-back pairs and rounds UP as often as down — 4.5 yields 6.0s. Ask for a multiple of 3.
A plate must be a LIFTED PANEL, not a transparent rect, or dark art has nothing to read against.

Over a graded still, thin outline scaffolding is not on screen. .30/.52 of a 2-3px stroke at 0.4 alpha survives no encode — draw with SOLID FILLS and strokes of 9px and up, and let the ghost/track shapes be filled rects at ~.2 rather than outlines.

tools/chapter_sheet.py samples a non-Lottie scene at +2.6s. A drawn layer that finishes at +4.4 sheets as a half-built frame and reads as a defect that is not one — assemble the mechanism by about +3.3, or judge that scene from the mp4.
chapter_design.generator: tools/chapter_project.py — builds a chapter project from the shipped cut + a hand-authored chapter.json. Every data-start / data-duration / data-framings / data-track-index, every on-screen string, every .bg and every <audio> row is lifted VERBATIM and only rebased; the spec owns the DESIGN only. It re-reads what it wrote and asserts the rebase before exiting, so a chapter whose durations sum correctly while its internal cuts drift cannot be produced.
chapter_design.one_root_html: A chapter project has exactly ONE root .html and it is index.html. `hyperframes check` only looks for index.html, tools/chapter_sheet.py hardcodes it, and the linter's `multiple_root_compositions` is an ERROR on two root files carrying data-composition-id — so the ch1/ch2 index.html + index-claudedesign.html pair cannot pass a check. In a chapter project index.html is NOT the shipped cut.
chapter_design.measure_position: `.measure-lab.under` / `.measure.under` — left calc(50% - 460px), top 868/910, width 920, height 7. Declared in the stylesheet, not per scene: at the old y742 the bar landed on the icon that variant-A scenes carry inside their stack, and struck its own label through on three consecutive frames of ch4.

social-quote.use: Quote a REAL, topical social post (X or Reddit) inside a scene when one genuinely relates to the video's argument. A component, never a whole architecture, and never fabricated — an invented post is a fabricated fact and breaks the never-invent rule.
social-quote.caution: Real posts mean real usernames and real people on screen. Prefer posts from institutional or public accounts; do not put a private individual's handle in a monetised video criticising their money decisions.

packaging._note: Packaging gates for Money Mavens (creator plan 2026-08-15). fin-package enforces these; the slate records the score that passed. Prose: vault/knowledge/niches/moneymavens-launch-slate.md.
packaging._title_score_min_note: A REAL return from vidiq_score_title, never rounded and never estimated. Below 75, regenerate — do not proceed. Score with the FINISHED script summary as the `description`: titles score better when the tool can see what the video contains, which is why 20 of the 30 slate titles were deliberately left unscored until production. A high score on a promise the script cannot keep still fails fact-integrity gate 8 — the SS-taxation cluster had all eight generated options rejected that way.
packaging._thumbnail_note: From vidiq_similar_thumbnails, US, 3-month window, across the 50K-500K view cluster of small US senior-finance channels: ONE concrete object (a form, a card, a bank window, a table) - not a person, not a chart; exactly ONE red element; 2-4 words that never repeat the title; no emoji, no brackets; high contrast, cool background, warm subject. ALL-CAPS works in this niche (Rd07Bc_Q0LM, 257,650 views) but one word per thumbnail at most.
packaging.intent_alternation: search, browse, browse, search, browse, search — never two browse videos back to back in the first month. Search builds the durable floor; browse supplies the spikes that feed it.

fact_gate._note: The ten-point pre-publish gate. Canonical prose + the source whitelist: vault/knowledge/fact-integrity.md §8 and §1. ANY single failure blocks publish; fin-audit owns it.
fact_gate._as_of_note: Every on-screen figure carries 'as of [Month Year]' ON THE FRAME that shows it. Not the description, not a closing card.
fact_gate._labels_note: Three-label discipline, on screen AND in script (fact-integrity §3). A label must never drift mid-sentence — split the sentence instead. An `estimate` shows the word example/illustration in frame plus its inputs.
fact_gate._expiry_note: annual = re-verify every January (IRS brackets, contribution limits, COLA, Part B premium, IRMAA, earnings test). monthly = re-verify before every publish that uses it (CPI, fed funds, Treasury yields, FDIC rate caps, saving rate). stable = re-verify annually (FDIC limit per category, FCRA retention, RMD age + Uniform Lifetime Table). An annually-expiring number inside an evergreen video is the #1 stale-content complaint driver.
fact_gate._indirection_note: A video links to CLAIMS; claims link to SOURCES. Never video -> source. That indirection is the whole mechanism: when one document expires, every dependent claim surfaces, and through them every video.
fact_gate.disclaimer: This video is general financial education, not financial, tax, or legal advice. No specific product, fund, bank, or provider is recommended. Figures are current as of the date shown on screen and change over time. Confirm anything that affects your own decision with the issuing agency or a licensed professional.
fact_gate._disclaimer_note: All four required. spoken = within the first 45s if any figure appears before then. onscreen = lower third at the FIRST dollar figure. description = above the fold, before the chapters. pinned = on any video touching taxes, Medicare, or Social Security claiming. Additions: 'Confirm with a tax professional' (tax) / 'Confirm with Medicare.gov or SHIP, your state's free Medicare counseling program' (Medicare).

source_screenshot._note: Screenshot-the-source is a DISTINCT asset class from stock photography (fact-integrity §4) and the stock rules do not apply to it. Screen-record the REAL government page — never rebuild the table in a graphics tool, which is exactly what layout.image_relevance would otherwise push you toward.
source_screenshot._min_hold_note: 3s is the floor for reading one row. Checked this against the build gate rather than assuming a conflict: check_build enforces scene.max_scene_seconds (9.0s), which 3s clears easily — scene.max_static_hold_seconds (2.0) is MOTION GUIDANCE and is not machine-enforced anywhere. So no exemption is needed. What the 2.0 does tell you still applies: a source shot must carry motion (the row highlight arriving, a slow push) or it reads as a dead frame. Hold the page, animate the highlight.
source_screenshot._highlight_note: Exactly ONE row or line highlighted. Never annotate more than one thing — a second annotation is the frame arguing with itself.
